problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=[\begin{aligned}\sqrt{t+1} \\ {e}^{t} \\ 2t\end{aligned}].$

activity_context.topic_title: The Domain of a Vector-Valued Function

feedback.problem: Find the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)=\sqrt{2t+4}\,i+({3}^{t}+{t}^{3})\,j+\frac{1}{t+2}\,k.$
feedback.worked_solution:
To find the domain of $f$, we need the intersection of the domains of the individual components.

- The domain of the 1st component $\sqrt{2t+4}$ is $t\in [-2,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 2nd component ${3}^{t}+{t}^{3}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$

- The domain of the 3rd component $\frac{1}{t+2}$ is $t\in (-\infty ,-2)\cup (-2,\infty ).$

The intersection is illustrated in the diagram below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14076578/assets/51c8f87355b42610cd67ce1651543c462f7ea4a980202844e9940514f431b412.png)

Therefore, the domain of the vector-valued function $f(t)$ is $t\in (-2,\infty ).$
